description:
## Why

The JMAP session object (GET /jmap/session) currently returns a hardcoded singleton account. With multiuser, it must return the authenticated user's own account ID, display name, and capabilities. SINGLETON_USER_ID is removed in this issue.

## What

- Remove SINGLETON_USER_ID = 1 from server.rs
- Session handler reads the authenticated username, resolves to user_id via the users table, and builds the session object dynamically:
  - accountId = u_{username}
  - name = display_name from users table
  - isPersonal = true
  - isReadOnly = false
  - capabilities = the standard RFC 8620 + RFC 8621 capability map
- primaryAccounts maps each capability URI to the user's accountId
- Admin users additionally see an admin accountId with admin capabilities

## Acceptance

- GET /jmap/session returns the correct accountId for each authenticated user
- Two users authenticated simultaneously see different session objects
- SINGLETON_USER_ID is gone from the codebase
- Existing session endpoint tests updated to reflect dynamic account ID
notes: JMAP account_id convention: u_{username}. This must match the convention used in JMAP request routing (stoa-jmap-accountid-routing) and in the Graph sync bridge (stoa-oxv8c).
title: JMAP session endpoint returns per-user account
